root_cause.text: The option walkers in `tcp_find_option` and `dccp_find_option` fail to check if `i` is at the last byte of the option area before reading `op[i+1]` to determine the option length, causing an out-of-bounds read when the final byte is a non-single-byte option kind.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds the condition `|| i == optlen - 1` before the branch that accesses `op[i+1]`, preventing the dereference when `i` is the last byte. The CVE description explicitly states "walkers that advance with i += op[i + 1] ? : 1 can read op[i + 1] past the end of the option area."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix out-of-bounds access in DCCP option parsing by guarding against reading beyond the buffer when on the last byte.
intent_record.what: Added a condition to check if `i` is the last byte of the option buffer (`i == optlen - 1`) in the inner `if` statement, and reformatted the ternary operator in the else branch to include spaces.
intent_record.how: The change prevents an out-of-bounds read when processing DCCP options: if the current byte indicates an option length less than 2 and it is the last byte of the buffer, it avoids accessing `op[i+1]` in the else branch. The reformatting of the ternary operator is cosmetic and does not affect functionality.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential out-of-bounds read in TCP option parsing when the last byte is a multi-byte option.
intent_record.what: Changed the loop increment logic in tcp_find_option: added condition '|| i == optlen - 1' to the if statement that decides whether to increment i by 1 or by op[i+1]; also reformatted the ternary operator.
intent_record.how: Prevents out-of-bounds access when i is at the last byte of the options buffer; when i == optlen - 1, the function now increments i by 1 instead of attempting to read op[i+1] which would be out of bounds.
